stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that its velocity vector at time t is \( v(t) = \left\langle 3 \cos{\left(t \right)},\ 2 t^{2} - 4 \right\rangle \). Using a calculator, find the total distance traveled by the particle over the time interval \( 0 \le t \le \frac{5}{2} \). Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The speed of the particle is the magnitude of its velocity, \( \lVert v(t) \rVert = \sqrt{\left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)^2 + \left(2 t^{2} - 4\right)^2} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: speed as the magnitude of velocity

worked_solution.text: The total distance is the integral of speed over the interval, \( \int_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}} \sqrt{\left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)^2 + \left(2 t^{2} - 4\right)^2}\,dt \), which a calculator gives as about 9.190.
worked_solution.rule_named: total distance as the integral of speed

options.derivation: the speed written without its square root, so the integrand is x'(t)^2 + y'(t)^2
the net change in position reported, the length of the displacement vector from the integrals of the two components
distance written as two separate one-dimensional distances added together, the integral of |x'(t)| plus the integral of |y'(t)|
